    The platform is an open, evidence-based educational resource dedicated to advancing scientific knowledge in peptide biology, synthesis chemistry, analytical characterization, and metabolic research.

!!! info "Executive Summary"
    BPC-157 is a synthetic pentadecapeptide (15 amino acids) derived from a stable protein fragment isolated from human gastric juice.

## Quick Facts
- **Sequence**: Gly-Glu-Pro-Pro-Pro-Gly-Lys-Pro-Ala-Asp-Asp-Ala-Gly-Leu-Val
- **Molecular Weight**: $\\approx 1419 \\text{ Da}$
- **Primary Research Focus**: Gastrointestinal protection, angiogenesis, tendon and muscle repair.

---

# Retatrutide Research Profile

!!! info "Executive Summary"
    Retatrutide (LY3437943) is an investigational synthetic peptide engineered as a triple agonist at the GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon (GCG) receptors.

## Quick Facts
- **Peptide Class**: Multi-Receptor Agonist (Triple Agonist)
- **Molecular Targets**: GLP-1R, GIPR, GCGR
- **Half-Life**: $\approx 6-7 \text{ days}$

## Mechanism of Action
Simultaneous activation of GLP-1R (appetite suppression), GIPR (lipid buffering), and GCGR (energy expenditure & hepatic lipid oxidation) produces synergistic weight loss and metabolic improvements.

<!-- FILE: peptide-library/semaglutide.md -->
---
title: "Semaglutide Research Profile"
description: "GLP-1 receptor agonist for metabolic research — molecular formula C187H291N45O59, MW 4,113 Da."
---

# Semaglutide Research Profile

!!! info "Executive Summary"
    Semaglutide is a 31-amino acid synthetic peptide analog of human glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) engineered for extended pharmacokinetic profile and resistance to dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) degradation.

## Quick Facts
- **Peptide Class**: GLP-1 Receptor Agonist
- **Molecular Target**: GLP-1 Receptor (GLP-1R)
- **Molecular Formula**: $C_{187}H_{291}N_{45}O_{59}$
- **Molecular Weight**: $4113.58 \text{ Da}$
- **Half-Life**: $\approx 7 \text{ days}$ (subcutaneous)

## Mechanism of Action
Semaglutide binds to the GLP-1 receptor, a class B G protein-coupled receptor expressed on pancreatic beta cells, central neurons, gastrointestinal cells, and cardiovascular tissues. Upon ligand binding, the receptor activates intracellular $G_{\alpha s}$ signaling, leading to increased cyclic AMP (cAMP) production and downstream activation of PKA and EPAC.

## Frequently Asked Questions
### What is the molecular basis for semaglutide's extended half-life?
Semaglutide incorporates a C18 fatty diacid attached via a glutamic acid linker to lysine at position 26. This fatty acid chain binds non-covalently to serum albumin, protecting the peptide from renal clearance and enzymatic degradation.

---

---

# Tirzepatide Research Profile

!!! info "Executive Summary"
    Tirzepatide (LY3298176) is a synthetic 39-amino acid peptide engineered as a first-in-class dual agonist of the glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptors.

## Quick Facts
- **Peptide Class**: Dual GIP/GLP-1 Receptor Agonist
- **Molecular Targets**: GIPR and GLP-1R
- **Amino Acid Length**: 39 amino acids
- **Half-Life**: $\approx 5 \text{ days}$

## Mechanism of Action
Tirzepatide simultaneously activates both GIP and GLP-1 receptors. GIPR signaling in adipose tissue and beta cells complements GLP-1R activation, producing superior glycemic control and weight reduction compared to selective GLP-1R agonists.

---

<!-- FILE: coa-guide/01-understanding-lc-ms-reports.md -->
---
title: "Understanding LC-MS Reports for Research Peptides"
description: "A comprehensive guide to reading Liquid Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (LC-MS) reports, interpreting m/z spectra, and verifying peptide molecular weight."
category: "Quality Control"
tags: [LC-MS, Mass Spectrometry, Molecular Weight, Peptide Identity]
author: "RPL Peptides Research Team"
published: "2026-08-01"
---

# Understanding LC-MS Reports for Research Peptides

!!! info "Executive Summary"
    Liquid Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (LC-MS) is the gold standard for confirming peptide molecular identity. While HPLC measures relative chromatographic purity, LC-MS measures the exact mass-to-charge ratio ($m/z$) of ionized molecules.

## ESI-MS Ionization Fundamentals
In Electrospray Ionization (ESI), peptides accept protons ($H^+$) during nebulization, forming multiply charged species in the gas phase:

$$\\frac{m}{z} = \\frac{M + z \\cdot 1.007276}{z}$$

Where:
- $M$ is the monoisotopic molecular mass of the neutral peptide.
- $z$ is the integer charge state ($+1, +2, +3, \\dots$).
- $1.007276$ is the mass of a proton ($H^+$).

### Example Charge State Calculation
For a peptide with monoisotopic mass $M = 4111.91\\text{ Da}$ (such as Semaglutide):
- $[M+3H]^{3+} = \\frac{4111.91 + 3(1.0073)}{3} = 1371.64\\text{ } m/z$
- $[M+4H]^{4+} = \\frac{4111.91 + 4(1.0073)}{4} = 1028.98\\text{ } m/z$

---

## TIC vs XIC Chromatograms

- **Total Ion Chromatogram (TIC)**: Plots total ion signal intensity across all scanned $m/z$ ratios against time.
- **Extracted Ion Chromatogram (XIC)**: Filters exclusively for $m/z$ signals corresponding to the calculated target peptide mass, isolating the analyte from background noise.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is the difference between Monoisotopic Mass and Average Mass?
Monoisotopic mass is calculated using the exact mass of the most abundant naturally occurring isotope for each element ($^{1}H, ^{12}C, ^{14}N, ^{16}O, ^{32}S$). Average mass is calculated using atomic weights averaged over natural isotopic abundances. High-resolution LC-MS reports monoisotopic mass.

---

---
title: "HPLC Chromatogram Interpretation: A Practical Field Guide"
description: "Learn how to read baseline stability, signal-to-noise ratio (S/N), ghost peaks, and solvent fronts on peptide HPLC chromatograms."
category: "Chromatography"
tags: [HPLC, Chromatogram, Baseline, Analytical Testing]
author: "RPL Peptides Research Team"
published: "2026-08-01"
---

# HPLC Chromatogram Interpretation: A Practical Field Guide

!!! info "Executive Summary"
    A chromatogram is a graphical plot of detector response versus time. Interpreting a chromatogram requires evaluating peak symmetry, baseline noise, and signal resolution.

## Signal-to-Noise Ratio ($S/N$) Formula

$$\\text{S/N} = \\frac{2H}{h}$$

Where:
- $H$ is the peak height from the central baseline to the apex.
- $h$ is the peak-to-peak noise range of the baseline observed in a blank run over a defined window.

According to ICH Q2(R2) guidelines:
- **Limit of Detection (LOD)**: $S/N \\ge 3:1$
- **Limit of Quantitation (LOQ)**: $S/N \\ge 10:1$

---

## Key Features of a Peptide Chromatogram

1. **Solvent Front ($t_0$)**: Initial void peak representing unretained mobile phase and non-retained salts.
2. **Main Target Peak**: Dominant signal representing the primary peptide product.
3. **Impurity Peaks**: Smaller secondary peaks corresponding to deletion sequences, diastereomers, or oxidation products.
4. **Baseline Drift**: Gradual upward or downward slope caused by gradient mobile phase absorbance changes.

---

<!-- FILE: coa-guide/03-peak-area-vs-peak-height.md -->
---
title: "Peak Area vs Peak Height in HPLC Purity Calculations"
description: "Discover why chromatographic peak area integration is mathematically required for peptide purity calculations instead of peak height."
category: "Analytical Chemistry"
tags: [Peak Area, Peak Height, HPLC Purity, Integration]
author: "RPL Peptides Research Team"
published: "2026-08-01"
---

# Peak Area vs Peak Height in HPLC Purity Calculations

!!! info "Executive Summary"
    Chromatographic purity calculations use integrated peak area rather than peak height because peak height varies significantly with column degradation, flow rate fluctuations, and band broadening.

## Mathematical Integration Formula

$$\\text{Area } (A) = \\int_{t_1}^{t_2} I(t) \\, dt$$

Where $I(t)$ is the detector intensity at time $t$, integrated between peak start $t_1$ and peak end $t_2$.

For a Gaussian chromatographic peak:

$$\\text{Area} \\approx H \\times W_{0.5}$$

Where $H$ is peak height and $W_{0.5}$ is peak width at half-height.

---

## Why Peak Height Fails for Purity Determination

As an analytical column ages, band broadening increases peak width while reducing peak height. However, the total number of absorbed photons (and thus total integrated peak area) remains constant for a fixed mass of analyte.

| Factor | Effect on Peak Height | Effect on Peak Area |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Column Aging** | Decreases | Remains Constant |
| **Flow Rate Decrease** | Increases | Remains Constant |
| **Temperature Increase** | Increases | Remains Constant |

---

---
title: "Retention Time (RT) Explained: Capacity Factor, Selectivity, and Drift"
description: "Understand the physicochemical factors governing peptide retention time (RT), capacity factor k', and retention time matching (HPLC-RTM)."
category: "Chromatography"
tags: [Retention Time, Capacity Factor, HPLC-RTM, Chromatography]
author: "RPL Peptides Research Team"
published: "2026-08-01"
---

# Retention Time (RT) Explained: Capacity Factor, Selectivity, and Drift

!!! info "Executive Summary"
    Retention time ($t_R$) measures how long an analyte is retained inside the chromatographic column. Capacity factor ($k'$) normalizes retention relative to system dead time ($t_0$).

## Capacity Factor (Retention Factor) $k'$ Formula

$$k' = \\frac{t_R - t_0}{t_0}$$

Where:
- $t_R$ is the retention time of the main peptide peak.
- $t_0$ is the column void time (time required for an unretained compound to pass through).

An optimal $k'$ value for analytical peptide chromatography ranges between $2.0 \\le k' \\le 10.0$.

---

## Causes of Retention Time Drift

- **Column Temperature Variations**: A $1^\\circ\\text{C}$ temperature change can alter $t_R$ by $1-3\\%$.
- **Mobile Phase Evaporation**: Volatile organic modifier loss alters gradient strength.
- **Column Aging & Silanol Exposure**: Stationary phase degradation shifts retention behavior over time.

---

---

# Common Synthetic Peptide Impurities: Types, Causes, and Detection

!!! info "Executive Summary"
    Synthetic peptide impurities arise from incomplete coupling reactions, side reactions during cleavage, or environmental degradation.

## Main Impurity Categories

| Impurity Type | Mechanism / Cause | Mass Shift | Chromatographic Behavior |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Deletion Peptides $(N-1)$** | Incomplete Fmoc coupling step | $-\\text{Mass of amino acid}$ | Elutes near target peak |
| **Oxidized Peptides** | Methionine/Tryptophan oxidation | $+16\\text{ Da } (\\text{or } +32\\text{ Da})$ | Earlier elution (more polar) |
| **Diastereomers** | Epimerization at $\\alpha$-carbon | $0\\text{ Da}$ (Identical Mass) | Partially resolved peak |
| **TFA Adducts** | Residual trifluoroacetic acid | $+114\\text{ Da}$ | Variable |

---

# USP <621> Chromatography Guide: Allowable Method Adjustments

!!! info "Executive Summary"
    USP <621> specifies acceptable tolerances for adjusting HPLC parameters without re-validating the analytical method.

## Summary of Allowable Adjustments

- **Column Length ($L$) / Particle Size ($d_p$)**: $L/d_p$ ratio may be adjusted within $-25\\%$ to $+50\\%$.
- **Flow Rate**: May be adjusted by $\\pm 50\\%$.
- **Column Temperature**: May be adjusted by $\\pm 10^\\circ\\text{C}$ (up to a maximum of $60^\\circ\\text{C}$).
- **pH of Mobile Phase**: May be adjusted by $\\pm 0.2\\text{ pH units}$.
- **Injection Volume**: May be reduced as long as detection precision and $S/N$ criteria are satisfied.

---

title: "ICH Q2(R2) Explained: Validation of Analytical Procedures"
description: "Breakdown of the ICH Q2(R2) guideline for analytical method validation in peptide quality control."

author: "RPL Peptides Research Team"
published: "2026-08-01"
---

# ICH Q2(R2) Explained: Validation of Analytical Procedures

!!! info "Executive Summary"
    ICH Q2(R2) defines global standards for validating analytical methods across core criteria: Specificity, Linearity, Accuracy, Precision, LOD, LOQ, and Robustness.

## Validation Criteria Matrix

| Validation Parameter | Acceptance Threshold | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Specificity** | Resolution $R_s \\ge 1.5$ from impurities | Ensures no co-eluting peaks |
| **Linearity** | $R^2 \\ge 0.999$ | Verifies proportional response |
| **Repeatability** | Peak Area $\\text{RSD} \\le 1.0\\%$ | Evaluates intra-day precision |
| **Intermediate Precision** | Peak Area $\\text{RSD} \\le 2.0\\%$ | Evaluates inter-day/analyst precision |

---

<!-- FILE: coa-guide/08-hplc-method-validation.md -->
---
title: "HPLC Method Validation Protocol for Research Peptide Quality Control"
description: "Practical step-by-step SOP for executing HPLC analytical method validation for research peptides."
category: "Method Validation"
tags: [SOP, Validation Protocol, Spike Recovery, Solution Stability]
author: "RPL Peptides Research Team"
published: "2026-08-01"
---

# HPLC Method Validation Protocol for Research Peptide Quality Control

!!! info "Executive Summary"
    Method validation ensures an HPLC analytical procedure consistently yields accurate, precise, and specific purity measurements for research peptides.

## Standard Validation Protocol Steps

1. **Solution Stability Testing**: Verify sample stability in autosampler at $4^\\circ\\text{C}$ over $24\\text{ h}$ and $48\\text{ h}$.
2. **Spike Recovery (Accuracy)**: Evaluate recovery across $80\\%$, $100\\%$, and $120\\%$ target concentrations (acceptance: $98.0\% - 102.0\%$).
3. **Linearity Range**: Assess detector response across $50\\%$ to $150\\%$ of nominal test concentration.

title: "System Suitability Testing (SST) in Peptide HPLC Analysis"
description: "Learn the acceptance criteria for HPLC System Suitability Testing (SST) prior to sample analysis."

---

# System Suitability Testing (SST) in Peptide HPLC Analysis

!!! info "Executive Summary"
    System Suitability Testing (SST) confirms instrument performance (pump, column, detector) prior to running production batch samples.

## Standard Acceptance Criteria

- **Peak Area Repeatability**: $\\text{RSD} \\le 1.0\\%$ ($n = 5$ or $6$ injections)
- **Retention Time Repeatability**: $\\text{RSD} \\le 0.5\\%$
- **Tailing Factor ($T$)**: $T \\le 1.5$
- **Chromatographic Resolution ($R_s$)**: $R_s \\ge 1.5$ between critical pair

<!-- FILE: coa-guide/10-analytical-method-transfer.md -->
---
title: "Analytical Method Transfer: Ensuring Inter-Laboratory Reproducibility"
description: "Best practices for transferring HPLC analytical procedures between testing facilities while maintaining data integrity."
category: "Quality Assurance"
tags: [Method Transfer, Inter-Laboratory, Dwell Volume, Reproducibility]
author: "RPL Peptides Research Team"
published: "2026-08-01"
---

# Analytical Method Transfer: Ensuring Inter-Laboratory Reproducibility

!!! info "Executive Summary"
    Method transfer verifies that a receiving laboratory can reproduce analytical purity results within pre-defined acceptance limits.

## Key Considerations in Transfer Protocols

1. **Dwell Volume ($V_D$) Matching**: Differences in system gradient delay volume ($V_D$) cause retention shifts in gradient elution.
2. **Column Lot-to-Lot Variability**: Stationary phase bonding density differences across C18 silica batches.
3. **Acceptance Criteria**: Mean purity difference between sending and receiving labs must be $\\le 0.5\\%$.

---

<!-- FILE: coa-guide/11-reverse-phase-hplc-for-peptides.md -->
---
title: "Reverse Phase HPLC for Peptides: Columns, Mobile Phases, and Ion-Pairing"
description: "Master Reversed-Phase HPLC (RP-HPLC) for peptide separation, silica pore sizes, C18 vs C4 phases, and TFA ion-pairing."
category: "Chromatography"
tags: [RP-HPLC, C18, Pore Size, Ion-Pairing, TFA]
author: "RPL Peptides Research Team"
published: "2026-08-01"
---

# Reverse Phase HPLC for Peptides: Columns, Mobile Phases, and Ion-Pairing

!!! info "Executive Summary"
    Reversed-Phase HPLC separates peptides based on hydrophobic interactions between side chains and non-polar stationary phases (C18, C8, C4).

## Pore Size Requirements

For peptides ($>2000\\text{ Da}$), **$300\\,\\text{\\AA}$ pore silica columns** are required to prevent restricted diffusion inside column pores. $100\\,\\text{\\AA}$ pore columns cause peak broadening and mass overload for larger peptides.

## Standard Mobile Phase System

- **Mobile Phase A**: $99.9\%\\text{ } H_2O + 0.1\%\\text{ TFA}$
- **Mobile Phase B**: $99.9\%\\text{ ACN} + 0.1\%\\text{ TFA}$

Trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) acts as an ion-pairing agent, masking basic amine charges and sharpening peak shapes.

---

<!-- FILE: coa-guide/12-tailing-factor-explained.md -->
---
title: "Tailing Factor Explained: Calculation, Causes, and Mitigation"
description: "Learn how to calculate tailing factor (T) and asymmetry factor (As), identify silanol interaction, and eliminate peak tailing."
category: "Peak Symmetry"
tags: [Tailing Factor, Peak Asymmetry, Silanol, Peak Shape]
author: "RPL Peptides Research Team"
published: "2026-08-01"
---

# Tailing Factor Explained: Calculation, Causes, and Mitigation

!!! info "Executive Summary"
    Peak tailing reduces chromatographic resolution and integration accuracy. Tailing factor ($T$) measures peak symmetry at $5\\%$ peak height.

## Tailing Factor Formula ($T$)

$$T = \\frac{W_{0.05}}{2f}$$

Where:
- $W_{0.05}$ is the total peak width at $5\\%$ of peak height.
- $f$ is the distance from peak apex to leading edge at $5\\%$ height.

An ideal Gaussian peak has $T = 1.0$. Acceptable SST limits specify $T \\le 1.5$.

---

<!-- FILE: coa-guide/13-resolution-in-chromatography.md -->
---
title: "Resolution in Chromatography: Formula, Peak Overlap, and Optimization"
description: "Understand chromatographic resolution (Rs), Purnell equation, and how baseline separation impacts reported purity."
category: "Chromatography"
tags: [Resolution, Purnell Equation, Peak Overlap, Separation]
author: "RPL Peptides Research Team"
published: "2026-08-01"
---

# Resolution in Chromatography: Formula, Peak Overlap, and Optimization

!!! info "Executive Summary"
    Chromatographic resolution ($R_s$) measures the degree of separation between two adjacent peaks. Baseline separation requires $R_s \\ge 1.5$.

## Resolution Formula

$$R_s = \\frac{2(t_{R2} - t_{R1})}{W_1 + W_2}$$

Where:
- $t_{R1}, t_{R2}$ are retention times of peaks 1 and 2.
- $W_1, W_2$ are baseline peak widths.

---
title: "Deletion Peptides Explained: Synthesis Mechanisms and Separation"
description: "Learn how (N-1) deletion peptides form during incomplete SPPS coupling steps and how RP-HPLC separates them from the main peak."
category: "Impurities"
tags: [Deletion Peptides, SPPS, Coupling Efficiency, HPLC Separation]
author: "RPL Peptides Research Team"
published: "2026-08-01"
---

# Deletion Peptides Explained: Synthesis Mechanisms and Separation

!!! info "Executive Summary"
    Deletion peptides $(N-1)$ lack one or more amino acid residues due to incomplete coupling reactions during Solid-Phase Peptide Synthesis (SPPS).

## Mass Shift ($\\Delta m$)
A deletion peptide missing a Valine residue exhibits a mass shift of $\\Delta m = -99.07\\text{ Da}$. On reversed-phase HPLC, deletion peptides typically elute very close to the target peak, requiring shallow gradients for baseline resolution ($R_s \\ge 1.5$).

<!-- FILE: coa-guide/15-oxidized-peptide-impurities.md -->
---
title: "Oxidized Peptide Impurities: Methionine, Tryptophan, and Cysteine"
description: "Examine oxidation pathways of sensitive amino acids in peptides and their characteristic chromatographic retention shifts."
category: "Impurities"
tags: [Oxidation, Methionine, Tryptophan, Degradation]
author: "RPL Peptides Research Team"
published: "2026-08-01"
---

# Oxidized Peptide Impurities: Methionine, Tryptophan, and Cysteine

!!! info "Executive Summary"
    Oxidation of Methionine to Methionine Sulfoxide increases molecule polarity, shifting retention time earlier on reversed-phase HPLC columns.

## Characteristic Mass Shift
- **Methionine Sulfoxide**: $+16\\text{ Da}$
- **Methionine Sulfone**: $+32\\text{ Da}$

Because sulfoxides introduce a polar oxygen atom, oxidized impurities elute **earlier** (smaller $t_R$) than the target peptide on C18 columns.

<!-- FILE: coa-guide/16-how-laboratories-calculate-hplc-purity.md -->
---
title: "How Laboratories Calculate HPLC Purity: Area Normalization vs External Standards"
description: "Detailed breakdown of Area Percent Normalization vs Weight/Weight Assay percentage in chromatographic quality control."
category: "Purity Calculation"
tags: [Area Normalization, Response Factor, Assay, HPLC Purity]
author: "RPL Peptides Research Team"
published: "2026-08-01"
---

# How Laboratories Calculate HPLC Purity: Area Normalization vs External Standards

!!! info "Executive Summary"
    Purity calculation method choice directly affects reported percentage values on a Certificate of Analysis (COA).

## Area Percent Normalization Formula

$$\\text{Purity (\\%)} = \\frac{A_{\\text{main}}}{\\sum_{i=1}^{n} A_i} \\times 100$$

## Corrected Purity with Relative Response Factors ($RRF$)

$$\\text{Corrected Purity (\\%)} = \\frac{\\frac{A_{\\text{main}}}{RRF_{\\text{main}}}}{\\sum_{i=1}^{n} \\frac{A_i}{RRF_i}} \\times 100$$

Where $RRF_i$ is the relative UV response factor of impurity $i$ at $214\\text{ nm}$ compared to the main peptide.

---

<!-- FILE: coa-guide/index.md -->
---
title: "HPLC vs HPLC-RTM in Peptide COA: Complete Guide to Reading Certificates of Analysis"
description: "Master peptide Certificate of Analysis (COA) interpretation. Learn how HPLC purity and HPLC-RTM are measured, peak integration, retention time, impurities, and why HPLC alone cannot verify identity."
keywords: "Peptide COA, HPLC Purity, HPLC-RTM, Retention Time, LC-MS, Peptide Quality Control, Chromatogram Integration"
---

# HPLC vs HPLC-RTM in Peptide COA: The Complete Guide to Reading Research Peptide Certificates of Analysis

!!! info "Executive Summary & Key Takeaways"
    - **Reported Purity $\neq$ Weight Percentage**: A reported HPLC purity of **99%** indicates that $99\%$ of UV-absorbing chromatographic peak area belongs to the main peak. It does not mean $99\%$ of the powder by net weight is peptide.
    - **HPLC $\neq$ Identity**: HPLC separates compounds by hydrophobicity but cannot confirm amino acid sequence or molecular weight. Definitive identity requires [Mass Spectrometry (LC-MS)](01-understanding-lc-ms-reports.md).
    - **HPLC-RTM (Retention Time Matching)**: Verifies that the sample elutes at the same retention time ($t_R$) as a verified reference standard under identical method conditions.

---

## 1. How Laboratories Calculate HPLC Purity

Chromatographic purity is determined by integrating the area under the detector response curve for all peaks detected above threshold:

$$\\text{Purity (\\%)} = \\frac{A_{\\text{main}}}{\\sum_{i=1}^{n} A_i} \\times 100$$

Where $A_{\\text{main}}$ is the peak area of the target peptide, and $\\sum A_i$ is the total peak area of all detected signals.

```text
Detector Signal (UV 214 nm)
^
|                         /\\  <-- Main Target Peak (Area: 99.12%)
|                        /  \\
|                       /    \\
|  /\\                  /      \\                 /\\
|_/  \\________________/        \\_______________/  \\_____> Retention Time (t_R)
  Impurity A                                    Impurity B
  (Area: 0.28%)                                (Area: 0.31%)
```

---

## 2. Key Differences: HPLC Purity vs HPLC-RTM

| Feature | HPLC Purity | HPLC-RTM (Retention Time Matching) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Primary Focus** | Relative peak area concentration | Retention behavior comparison |
| **Metric Used** | Integrated Peak Area ($A_{\\text{main}} / \\sum A_i$) | Retention Time ($t_R$) vs Reference ($t_{R,\\text{ref}}$) |
| **Acceptance Criteria** | $\\ge 95.0\\%$ or $\\ge 98.0\\%$ | $\\Delta t_R \\le \\pm 0.1\\text{ min}$ vs Reference |
| **What It Proves** | Absence of significant organic impurities | Chromatographic match with reference standard |
| **Limitation** | Ignores non-UV absorbing salts/water | Does not prove sequence or molecular weight |

---

## 3. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

### Does 99% HPLC purity mean the peptide is 99% pure by weight?
**No.** HPLC purity represents chromatographic peak area percentage under specific column, mobile phase, and UV detector wavelength conditions. It does not account for non-UV absorbing counterions (such as acetate or TFA salts), moisture, residual solvents, or inorganic salts. To determine absolute weight percentage, complementary assays such as Peptide Content (N-element analysis) or Gravimetric Analysis are required.

### Can HPLC retention time alone confirm peptide identity?
**No.** Retention time indicates how long a compound is retained by the column stationary phase. Two completely different peptides with similar hydrophobicity and amino acid composition can elute at nearly identical retention times. Definitive identity confirmation requires [Mass Spectrometry (LC-MS)](01-understanding-lc-ms-reports.md) or HRMS.

### Why do two independent laboratories report different retention times for the same batch?
Retention time is method-dependent. Differences in column dimensions, C18 stationary phase brand, gradient slope, flow rate, system dwell volume, and ambient temperature directly alter $t_R$. As long as the sample matches a qualified reference standard under the same method ([HPLC-RTM](04-retention-time-explained.md)), the data remains valid.

---

# What Are Peptides?

!!! info "Executive Summary"
    Peptides are short chains of amino acids linked by amide (peptide) bonds, typically ranging from 2 to 50 residues in length. They function as signaling molecules, hormones, neurotransmitters, and antimicrobial agents across biological systems.

---

# Biotechnology Applications of Peptides

!!! info "Executive Summary"
    Peptide biotechnology encompasses peptide-based materials, biosensors, peptide-drug conjugates (PDCs), and engineered biomaterials.

# Peptides in Cell Biology Research

!!! info "Executive Summary"
    Synthetic peptides enable precise manipulation of cell proliferation, differentiation, cell-matrix adhesion (RGD motif), and apoptosis in cell biology models.

# Peptides in Metabolic Research

!!! info "Executive Summary"
    Metabolic research peptides serve as tools to probe glucose homeostasis, thermogenesis, lipid partitioning, and energy expenditure pathways.

---

<!-- FILE: research/applications/molecular-biology-research.md -->
---
title: "Peptides in Molecular Biology Research"
description: "Peptide nucleic acids (PNAs), epitope tags, and enzyme substrate peptides."
---

# Peptides in Molecular Biology Research

!!! info "Executive Summary"
    Molecular biology uses peptide epitope tags (FLAG, HA, His6), PNAs for sequence-specific nucleic acid binding, and fluorogenic peptide substrates for enzyme kinetics.

---
[Return to Applications Overview](index.md)


---

<!-- FILE: research/applications/peptide-radiolabeling.md -->
---
title: "Peptide Radiolabeling"
description: "PET and SPECT radiopeptide imaging (68Ga, 18F) and PRRT therapy (177Lu)."
---

# Peptide Radiolabeling

!!! info "Executive Summary"
    Bifunctional chelators (DOTA, NOTA) attach radioactive isotopes (68Ga, 177Lu, 99mTc) to peptide vectors for diagnostic PET/SPECT imaging and targeted radionuclide therapy (theranostics).

---
[Return to Applications Overview](index.md)


---

<!-- FILE: research/applications/peptide-vaccines.md -->
---
title: "Peptide Vaccines"
description: "Synthetic epitope selection, multi-epitope designs, adjuvants, and neoantigen vaccines."
---

# Peptide Vaccines

!!! info "Executive Summary"
    Peptide vaccines deliver short synthetic T-cell and B-cell epitopes combined with TLR adjuvants to elicit targeted protective immune responses against pathogens or cancer neoantigens.

---
[Return to Applications Overview](index.md)


---

<!-- FILE: research/metabolic/gip-research.md -->
---
title: "GIP Research"
description: "Glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide biology and receptor signaling."
---

# GIP Research

!!! info "Executive Summary"
    GIP is a 42-amino acid incretin hormone secreted by K-cells that regulates insulin secretion, glucagon release, and lipid buffering in adipose tissue.

---
[Return to Metabolic Research Overview](index.md)


---

<!-- FILE: research/metabolic/glp-1-research-overview.md -->
---
title: "GLP-1 Research Overview"
description: "Incretin hormone biology, GLP-1 receptor activation, and cardiometabolic research."
---

# GLP-1 Research Overview

!!! info "Executive Summary"
    Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) is a 30/31-amino acid incretin hormone that stimulates glucose-dependent insulin secretion, suppresses glucagon, and promotes satiety.

---
[Return to Metabolic Research Overview](index.md)


---

<!-- FILE: research/metabolic/glp1-gip-dual-agonist.md -->
---
title: "GLP-1/GIP Dual Agonists"
description: "Unimolecular dual receptor agonism and synergistic metabolic targeting."
---

# GLP-1/GIP Dual Agonists

!!! info "Executive Summary"
    Dual GLP-1/GIP agonists like tirzepatide combine complementary incretin pathways in a single molecule, producing superior glycemic control and weight reduction compared to single-receptor agonists.

---
[Return to Metabolic Research Overview](index.md)


---

# Multi-Receptor Peptide Research
